newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian domestics seek shelter in embassy.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian domestics seek shelter in embassy.

text.p: Twenty-eight Indonesian domestic helpers were seeking refuge at the Indonesian embassy in Singapore because of alleged mistreatment by their employers, Indonesia's official Antara news agency reported on Tuesday.
"Some workers were locked up for months and made to work during the night," the agency quoted State Minister of Women's Affairs Mien Sugandhi as telling reporters in Singapore on Sunday.
In Singapore, a diplomat at the Indonesian embassy confirmed that 28 Indonesian domestic helpers were taking refuge there.
The diplomat, who declined to be identified, said some had complained that their wages were withheld and others said they had been raped by their employers.
He would give no further details.

Sugandhi, who had met 1,000 Indonesian domestic helpers working in Singapore, was quoted by Antara as saying many had complained that their wages were withheld although they had worked for several months.

She was quoted as saying there were also reports of domestic helpers being raped by their employers, adding that some of the women escaped from their employers' apartments by tying bed sheets together and climbing down the outside walls.
Sugandhi was on her way to the Middle East to obtain first-hand information on conditions there for Indonesian workers. Her first Middle East stop was the United Arab Emirates.
In early February, Anatara quoted her as saying she would "soon" visit Saudi Arabia to investigate allegations that Indonesian women were working there as prostitutes.
Several thousand Indonesians work in the Middle East, mainly as domestic helpers or labourers.
